sense: test what someone thinks, before asking outright

evidence: Cic. Clu. 176: animōs servōrum spē et metū (Lewis & Short s.v. tentō)
terms.comment: The verb is “to feel, handle, try”: of the pulse, vēnās temptāre (Quint. 11.3.88, Lewis & Short); of a person, to try what he will do or say.

sources: Lewis & Short: tento
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 98, 314.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
